'''''Aronia melanocarpa''''', called the '''black chokeberry''', is a species of [[shrub]]s in the [[Rosaceae|rose family]] native to eastern [[North America]], ranging from [[Canada]] to the central [[United States]], from [[Newfoundland]] [[west]] to [[Ontario]] and [[Minnesota]], [[south]] as far as [[Arkansas]], [[Alabama]], and [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]].<ref>{{BONAP |genus=Aronia |species=melanocarpa |date=2014}}</ref> This plant has been introduced and is cultivated in [[Europe]].

It is a branching shrub with glossy dark green [[leaves]] that take on a red color in the [[autumn]]; it grows well in the [[sun]] and part-shade, often to heights of six feet (1.8 m) or more, forming clumps by means of stems rising from the [[root]]s. Its [[flower]]s are white or pink, appearing at the end of [[Spring (season)|spring]] and producing black [[fruit]]s in September. The plants are relatively easy to clone and root, with summer being the optimal time to take cuttings. Some [[bird]]s eat the [[berries]].

When raw, the fruits are [[astringency|astringent]],<ref>{{eFloras|1|242416098|Aronia melanocarpa |family=Rosaceae |first=Richard J. |last=Pankhurst}}</ref> but the flavor improves when used in recipes with added sugar.

==Phytochemistry==

Aronia melanocarpa is notable for its rich phytochemical composition, particularly its high content of polyphenolic compounds. The fruit contains significant concentrations of anthocyanins, proanthocyanidins, and phenolic acids. Total phenolic content varies depending on cultivation, processing, and ripeness, placing the fruit among the plant sources with the highest recorded concentration of these chemical constituents. <ref>{{cite journal | author1 = Jurčević, Ivana Lončar | author2 = Rimac Brnčić, Sonja | author3 = Ščetar, Mario | title = Phenolic Content, Antioxidant Capacity and Quality of Chokeberry (Aronia melanocarpa) Products | journal = Croatian Journal of Food Science Technology | volume = 9 | issue = 2 | pages = 139-149 | year = 2017 | url = https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5068402/ }}</ref>
